question.problem: If $\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{5}{3}$ and $\frac{\pi }{2}<\theta <\pi $ then what is the value of $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ?$

current_example.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253560/assets/0c29b3961f3e1178f0c82680ca3f67904e57b6fe2cc8b887f09926fcf6c2149a.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that $\sin\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2},$ what is the value of $\tan\theta?$
current_example.worked_solution:
We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\cos\theta\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\sin\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{3}{4}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}} \\  & =\pm \frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $\cos\theta$ is positive in the fourth quadrant. So, $\cos\theta = \dfrac 1 2.$

Finally, knowing that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta},$ we have

$$
\tan\theta = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt 3}{2}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} =-\sqrt 3.
$$
